title: Introduce residency-assertion-enforcer and audit safety-net for cross-region KMS calls
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a residency assertion enforcer that validates KMS requests against tenant residency claims and an audit safety-net that stamps and stores evidence for fallback analysis.
description:
Context and motivation:
As customers adopt multi-region and sovereign deployments, we need stronger runtime checks to prevent inadvertent KMS usage outside a tenant's allowed geography and to ensure forensic evidence is captured when policy routing falls back. This change adds an in-process ResidencyAssertionEnforcer for the KMS proxy path and an audit-safety-net that records deterministic assertions when a request is routed outside the preferred region.

What this PR changes (summary):
- ResidencyAssertionEnforcer: middleware that validates - the request's tenant residency claim (from the token / tenant metadata) against the destination KMS region. If mismatch and no override, request is rejected with 403 and a structured error code (SEC_RESIDENCY_VIOLATION).
- RBAC v2 hook: Enforcer consults the RBAC v2 policy cache to ensure the calling principal has the kms:encrypt/kms:decrypt permission scoped to the target region.
- Audit safety-net: when automatic routing sends a request to an alternate region (configurable policy), the enforcer emits a signed audit envelope (immutable) with the assertion, original route decision, and policy fingerprint. Envelopes are sent to the audit-collector for retention and to support post-incident proofs.
- Tests: unit tests for the enforcer policy matrix, integration test exercising a simulated cross-region failover, and a lightweight e2e scenario that validates envelopes appear in the staging audit collector.
- Config: new config knobs (residency.enforcement = on|off|warn, residency.warn_threshold_seconds, residency.audit_bucket) and migration note.

Review conversation (selected highlights):
Elliot Chen (reviewer): "Overall this looks good; two concerns: 1) the envelope signer uses an HMAC key derived from the service key material — we should ensure it can't be misused for non-repudiation claims. 2) Tests assume the policy cache is warm. Please add a cold-cache test or document the behavior."

Maya Patel (author): "Thanks Elliot. I switched the signer to an envelope HMAC with limited scope (envelope_type + timestamp), and added a cold-cache unit test that simulates cache miss and ensures enforcement falls back to 'warn' mode when the feature flag is warn. Added a config comment explaining advisor behavior on cold cache."

Priya Rao (reviewer): "When enforcement is off but audit-safety-net is on, we still collect envelopes. We should make it clear in the runbook how to interpret envelopes that don't correspond to blocked requests."

Maya Patel: "Added explicit metadata field 'enforcement_mode' in the envelope payload (on|off|warn) and expanded the runbook note. Also added an observability gauge to reflect current enforcement mode for easier dashboarding."

Samir Gupta (security lead): "Approve with one requested change: add an access-control test where a tenant-scoped service principal attempts a cross-region call with kms:decrypt but lacks region scope; enforcer must return 403 and produce an envelope with reason=rbac_denied."

Maya Patel: "Added the access-control integration test (integration/tests/kms_rbac_denied_e2e.yaml) and validated locally."

Notes and roll-forward considerations:
- This PR intentionally keeps policy evaluation local and read-only; longer term we will add async policy reconciler to reduce cold-cache latency.
- We selected an HMAC-envelope approach to avoid heavy crypto dependencies in the critical path; if customers need stronger non-repudiation we will add signed envelopes using a KMS-backed signing key behind a dedicated endpoint.
